validation_notes: The chart shows a sharp decline from early June (~$6) down to a bottom around $2.5 by mid-July, followed by a long consolidation/basing period roughly between $2.5-3.0 through late July, and then a modest uptick to ~2.9-3.0 in early August. This looks more like a flat basing/bottoming range than a descending triangle. A descending triangle requires a clearly falling upper resistance line with lower highs converging into a flat support - but the recent price action (last 2-3 weeks) shows relatively flat highs and flat lows with a slight upward drift, not a converging wedge. There's no clear compression or narrowing range near the right edge; price recently broke slightly higher out of the range around $2.5-2.7 to ~2.9-3.0, suggesting a mild breakout upward rather than a triangle still forming. I don't see convincing lower-high touch points forming a descending trendline with 2+ clean touches converging toward apex on the right side.
